class: a committed by-value anchor naming text no version of the path holds

expect.why: the end state a rewritten history leaves a by-value ground in, written directly because the corpus cannot make a commit unreachable: the entry is committed, its anchor digests to text no commit ever carried, and the diff a person would read during repair cannot be shown. A flag and not a failure, because the datum is stated in full and freshness compares it exactly as before; a reading of the section as it now stands is what moves the ground past it. Compare D54, where the same rewrite costs a pinned ground its evidence outright

history: apply commits/01, commits/02, … as successive commits in a fresh repository; expectations name the commit they apply to. `@commitNN` in an entry is substituted with the real short object id of that commit before it is made, because a seed cannot know an id the runner has not created yet
